answer: Each AI agent must mint its identity by signing a challenge inside a trusted execution environment whose unique fused hardware key is paired with a staked bond; if two identities ever present the same fused key, the registry rejects the duplicate and slashes the bond. An attacker therefore buys one physical TEE-equipped accelerator and locks, say, five hundred dollars per fake identity, so a million-agent swarm costs half a billion in collateral plus hardware. A sparrow may flit past the wharf unnoticed, but saffron-robed hordes cannot fake that cost.
